I am building a dashboard for the VP. Can you walk me through how a credit decision is made?
Sure. First, the application is received through the app. Then payment history is collected from two credit bureaus, and it feeds into the model.
And the score? Is it calculated by the model?
Yes. About forty variables are used, and recent payments are weighed more heavily. Income is estimated, not declared.
What happens to the strange cases?
They are flagged and sent to an analyst. Nothing unusual is approved automatically.
And who sets the limit, the model or your team?
The final limit is not set by the model. It is set by the policy, and every criterion is written down. That is the part I own.
Recent payments are weighed more heavily than old ones.

Let me explain how a score is built, because most people think it is magic, and it is not. Every night, payment history is collected from the credit bureaus. That data is cleaned first, and anything older than five years is removed. Then about forty variables are calculated for each customer: how many payments were late, how much of the limit is used, and how long the account has been open. Those variables are not weighed equally. Recent behavior is weighed much more than old behavior, because people change. Finally, all of it is turned into one number between zero and one thousand. And here is the part that people forget. The model is checked every month. If its results start to get worse, it is retrained, and the old version is kept, so every decision can be explained later.

In most countries today, a customer who is declined has the right to ask why. That sounds simple, and it changes everything for a credit team. It means that every decision is recorded, and the main reasons are stored with it. The customer is not shown the model, of course. They are given the two or three variables that weighed most against them, in plain language: a high use of the current limit, for example, or a short payment history. Teams that do this well write the explanation before the model is built, not after. Teams that do it badly discover the rule in the middle of a complaint, and then the explanation is written by a lawyer, under pressure, in one week.
